sentences.text: Shri Santosh Kumar Meena - Advocate for the appellant.
Shri Bhaskar Agrawal - Govt. Advocate for the responden

Heard on I.A. No.9258/2025 which is first application under Section 430 of Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of suspension of remaining jail sentence filed on behalf of appellant - Vikram @ Ikram.
02.

The appellant has been convicted under Section 363, 366(A), 344, 376(2)(N) & 376(3) of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 3 years with fine of Rs.5,000/-, R.I. for 7 years with fine of Rs.5,000/-, R.I. for 3 years with fine of Rs.5,000/-, Life Imprisonment with fine of Rs.20,000/-
respectively, with default stipulation.

03. Counsel for the appellant argued that appellant has already remained in jail for more than 3 years, this is an appeal of year 2023, therefore, final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future.
He further argued that the Prosecutrix was a consenting party and

as per the prosecution,
age of the Prosecutrix was 14 years 1 month and 25 days as per the scholar register, but the prosecution has failed to prove the source on the basis of which the date of birth was recorded in the scholar register.

In support of his contention, learned counsel has placed reliance on a judgment passed by the Division Bench in the case of Tejubai V/s The State of Madhya Pradesh reported in 2025 (1) MPLJ (Crl.) 75, in which it has been 2 CRA-2606-2023 held that recording of the age of the prosecutrix cannot be the basis for conviction.

entities.text: Tejubai V/s The State of Madhya Pradesh reported in 2025 (1) MPLJ (Crl.) 75
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In such circumstances, his remaining jail sentence may be suspended.
04. Counsel for the respondent / State opposes the aforesaid application and prays for its rejection.

05. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the testimony of the Prosecutrix that she was a consenting party and apart from that the source of age of the Prosecutrix has not been mentioned by the witnesses and also considering the judgment passed by the Division Bench in the case of Tejubai V/s The State of Madhya Pradesh reported in 2025 (1) MPLJ (Crl.) 75,
Vikram @ Ikram vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 25 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3138534/
1 in which it has been held that recording of the age of the prosecutrix cannot be the basis for conviction and also considering that the appellant has already remained in jail for more than 3 years and this appeal is of year 2023, final hearing of this appeal will take time, we find prima facie case to grant suspension of jail sentence to the present appellant.

sentences.text: 06. Accordingly, I.A. No.9258/2025, is allowed and it is directed that subject to depositing fine amount and on furnishing personal bond by the appellant Vikram @ Ikram in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousands Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court and on deposit of fine amount (if not already deposited), the execution of custodial part of the jail sentence shall remain suspended, till the final disposal of this appeal.

The appellant after being enlarged on bail, shall mark his presence before the Registry of this 3 CRA-2606-2023 Court on 04.08.2026 and on all such subsequent dates as may be fixed by the Registry of this Court in this regard.

(VIJAY KUMAR SHUKLA) (ALOK AWAS  JUDGE JUDGE  Divyansh Vikram @ Ikram vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 25 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3138534/
